## 1) Run module autopilot (select best)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to verify afterward:
- A new “best” module set is selected (look for an updated “selected/best” pointer or an updated candidate record in the registry outputs).
- No regressions vs the current champion metrics you listed:
  - tuning_mean should ideally beat **3.5304** (lower is better only if your system defines it that way; otherwise compare in the expected direction)
  - lockbox_mean should ideally beat **4.0608**

If this step produces a new champion artifact, keep the old file `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` intact and ensure the system writes a new versioned champion (or at least a backup copy).

## 2) Run system autopilot (system candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to verify afterward:
- At least one system candidate completes fully (no “INCONCLUSIVE”/timeouts).
- The report includes comparable metrics to the champion (tuning + lockbox).
- If any candidate beats the champion on your selection criteria, confirm whether the tool automatically promotes it or only reports it.

## 3) Generate next fix plan
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What to verify afterward:
- `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` is created/updated.
- The suggested fixes align with the latest run artifacts (i.e., it’s not referencing stale candidates).

## If anything fails (quick triage checklist)
- Confirm the registry/spec paths exist:
  - `experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml`
  - `experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml`
- Re-run with whatever verbosity/log flag your tools support (often `--debug` or `--verbose`), and capture:
  - traceback
  - last ~200 lines of log
  - any “artifact path” it tried to read/write

If you paste the stdout/stderr from step (1) and step (2), I can tell you whether a new best was selected and what the next fix file is likely to recommend.
